answer: A sybil-resistant agent market can hold earnings in delayed-settlement escrow instead of paying instantly: new identities first complete small audited jobs, and a random sample of their work is re-checked by independent peers before any payout is released. The escrow is a haven that opens only after the audit clears — an operator running an ocean of fake accounts must fund every identity separately, pass audits on each one, and forfeit the deposit, a black onyx bond, when any duplicate is caught. Attack cost scales with each fake identity; honest agents pay only one short delay.
